text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds were little changed in late trade as dealers were divided on the near-term outlook for the market. Chart technical factors were expected to dominate on Friday with no major market-moving economic data expected in the U.S., and only producer price data due in Germany. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.89, up 0.01 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts closed higher after a day which saw little action, with many buyers sidelined ahead of next Tuesday's budget. Q3 GDP data and Q2 c/a data were in line with expectations, giving little domestic focus to the market. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-22/32, up 14/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures struggled to make ground despite a buoyant U.S. bond market as few wanted to take long positions after the relentless rally this month. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.64, down 0.06 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets make a late recovery ahead of preliminary Italian consumer prices data due after the market closed, but traders said the tone was bearish. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.25, down 0.05 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were largely unchanged at midday, as the market's morning rally was stopped in its tracks when it hit key technical resistance levels. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-18/32, down 5/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.41 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond futures contract ended the session sharply lower. It opened at the day's high of 125.05 on news that the Ministry of Finance had suspended most business operations of Hanwa Bank Ltd, a regional bank in western Japan. But JGB futures quickly turned lower on speculative selling by foreign players, remaining in negative territory for most of the day. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.48, down 0.57 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Other borrowers did their bit but Russia overshadowed other business with a $1.0 billion Eurobond. The spread was set at 345 b.p. rather than 350 b.p. to help shorten the order book and the allocation process. Distribution was said to be very well balanced. The European Investment Bank and Morgan Guaranty popped up in sterling ahead of next week's British budget.
